system: You generate realistic synthetic test data for a research benchmark about personal memory. Everything you write is fiction: invent every person, company, client and product name (never use real people you know of, and avoid famous companies as employers). Write like real life, not like a tidy diary: people get interrupted, leave things half done, revisit things, procrastinate, and type casually. Reply with JSON only.
user:
Invent one person for a 5-workday slice of their life. Archetype: student. Variety seed: student.
They live in the US Central time zone and use a Mac.

Return JSON:
{"persona": {"name", "role", "company" (invented), "summary", "workday": {"start": "HH:MM", "end": "HH:MM", "lunch": "HH:MM"}},
 "people": [{"key", "name" (invented, first+last unless family), "role", "channel"}],   // 5-9
 "threads": [{"key" (snake_case), "title", "kind": one of "main"|"decision"|"correspondence"|"side_project"|"personal",
              "arc": "how it develops over the 5 days, with concrete numbers/identifiers that change"}],  // 4-6
 "apps": [app keys they use, from: slack (Slack), vscode (Code), terminal (Terminal), xcode (Xcode), zoom (zoom.us), messages (Messages), mail (Mail), notes (Notes), chatgpt (ChatGPT), claude (Claude), spotify (Spotify), finder (Finder), figma (Figma), calendar (Calendar), preview (Preview), excel (Microsoft Excel), keynote (Keynote), notion (Notion)],
 "sites": [hosts they use for work and life, e.g. "docs.google.com", "mail.google.com", "github.com", "canvas.instructure.com"],
 "noise": {"slack_titles": [window titles if they use Slack], "pages": [{"host", "title", "path"}]}   // distractions
}
Threads must include a decision whose number or choice changes across days, a correspondence with someone outside
their team over email, and something personal. Include at least one concrete identifier (ticket, PR, order, invoice,
room, course code). Use Google Chrome for all websites.

persona.name: Maya Chen
persona.summary: Maya is a second-year master's student juggling a part-time research assistantship, a group project for her human-computer interaction seminar, and a side project building a small web app for a local nonprofit. She tends to start her day late, get distracted by social media and music, and then work in bursts. She is trying to be better about using her calendar and Notion to track tasks, but often falls back on sticky notes and her own memory.

people.name: Lila Thompson
people.role: Nonprofit contact at Open Streets Collective

threads.title: HCI group project: usability study of library wayfinding app
threads.arc: The group is preparing a usability test protocol for a mobile app concept. On Monday they debate whether to use moderated or unmoderated testing. Raj pushes for unmoderated to save time, Sophia wants moderated for richer data. They split the difference: 3 moderated pilot sessions on Wednesday, then 8 unmoderated sessions via UserTesting.com by Friday. The decision flips back and forth in Slack. By Thursday they have results: 2 critical usability issues (confusing back button, map zoom controls). They plan to present findings in class on Monday. Maya is assigned to write the methods section and keeps procrastinating until Friday evening.

threads.title: Research assistantship: transcription coding for lab
threads.arc: Maya works 10 hours/week for Dr. Okafor's lab coding interview transcripts. She has a batch of 5 transcripts to code in NVivo. On Monday she codes 2 transcripts, but gets bored and switches to other tasks. On Wednesday she realizes she coded one transcript with the wrong theme labels and has to redo it. She emails Dr. Okafor on Thursday asking for clarification on the 'community trust' code definition. He replies Friday morning with examples. She finishes the remaining 3 transcripts Friday afternoon and submits a summary to the lab's shared drive.

threads.title: Side project: web app for Open Streets Collective
threads.arc: Maya is building a simple event calendar and volunteer signup page for a local nonprofit. She uses React and Firebase. On Monday she deploys a beta to Netlify and sends the link to Lila. Lila replies Tuesday with feedback: the volunteer form doesn't have a 'dietary restrictions' field and the event dates are in the wrong timezone. Maya fixes the timezone bug Tuesday night, adds the dietary field Wednesday. She also creates a simple admin page to let Lila add events. On Friday she sends Lila a final test link and invoice for $400 (she quoted $350 but added $50 for the extra admin page). Lila says the nonprofit board needs to approve the invoice, will pay by next week.

threads.title: Course registration for next semester
threads.arc: Maya needs to decide between two electives: INFO 6501 'Data Visualization' and INFO 6502 'Critical AI Ethics'. She initially registers for Data Viz on Monday, then on Wednesday after talking to Priya (who took AI Ethics) she switches to Critical AI Ethics. On Thursday she checks RateMyProfessors and sees the AI Ethics professor has mixed reviews. She also realizes Data Viz conflicts with her planned lab hours. She finally decides to stick with AI Ethics and drops Data Viz on Friday. The course registration system shows a waitlist position of 3 for AI Ethics, but she gets in because she registered early.

threads.title: Email correspondence with Lila about web app
threads.arc: Maya and Lila exchange a series of emails about the Open Streets Collective web app. Monday: Maya sends the beta link. Tuesday: Lila sends feedback about the volunteer form and timezone. Wednesday: Maya replies that she's fixed the issues and asks for content (event descriptions, photos). Thursday: Lila sends a Google Drive folder with photos and event copy. Friday: Maya sends the final test link and invoice #2024-0317 for $400. Lila replies that the board will review it.

threads.title: Dad's birthday gift
threads.arc: Maya's dad's birthday is next week. She keeps meaning to buy him a gift. On Monday she searches for 'best gifts for dad who likes fishing' but gets distracted. On Wednesday she texts her dad to ask what he wants, he says 'nothing, just save your money'. She doesn't believe him. On Friday she orders a personalized tackle box from Etsy for $65. She texts Priya to ask if she thinks it's a good gift. Priya says yes. Maya feels relieved.
